answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake behind a verifiable, time-consuming proof of useful work before it may trade. Like a workshop that will not sell a marble countertop on credit to a stranger who has only just arrived, peers check stake and work history on the ledger. A walnut dealer and a timber merchant therefore trust only identities with sunk cost. Creating a thousand fakes then costs a thousand stakes plus a thousand work proofs, while honest agents pay once and keep trading, so scale gives the attacker no advantage.
